llm.summary: This skill openly provides high-trust Android phone automation, including screen reading and taps, with the main sensitive behavior disclosed and mostly scoped to user-directed use.

dimensions.detail: Control of any connected Android app is inherently high impact, and screenshots or accessibility dumps may contain personal or payment data; this is central to the purpose and disclosed, though the Appium fallback still uses predictable /tmp screenshot files in some paths.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a local Python virtualenv plus Android automation dependencies and an optional bridge start script; no hidden package manager abuse, sudo escalation, or broad system modification was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill includes a clear trigger boundary, tells agents not to act speculatively, requires confirmation before orders or checkout actions, and states that payment credentials are entered by the user and not stored.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The fallback bridge deliberately starts a long-lived Appium service and daemon, but it is documented, binds to localhost, uses private 0700/0600 IPC files, rejects foreign or group/world-writable command files, and does not enable Appium insecure modes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to read and control Android apps through OCR, accessibility, Appium, uiautomator2, taps, scrolling, and typing; the artifact code implements those same capabilities without unrelated exfiltration or destructive behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the agent live control of a connected Android phone. Use it for explicit tasks, review confirmations before purchases or account-changing taps, avoid entering payment secrets through the scripts, and clean or stop the bridge after use, especially on shared machines.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: The reported implementation defects are real reliability issues in the fallback path: one screenshot command does not check adb failures, and cmd_ocr_tap references an undefined driver after saving a screenshot. These should be fixed, but they do not show hidden or malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Screenshot, OCR, accessibility-tree reading, and clipboard use are expected for this phone-control skill and are disclosed. The primary OCR bridge uses a private cache directory, but fallback /tmp screenshots and raw clipboard text printed to stdout are avoidable local privacy exposures.
[RA2] expected: The persistent Appium and bridge daemon behavior is purpose-aligned and documented as a performance fallback. The IPC protections and localhost binding reduce the concern, though users should stop the bridge when finished.
